claims.text: Reducing the number of constituent elements from the equiatomic quinary alloy favors increased chemical short-range order in the single-phase FCC matrix.
Enhanced chemical short-range order locally increases lattice distortion.
The lattice distortions associated with chemical short-range order inhibit dislocation mobility.
Inhibited dislocation mobility increases yield strength relative to the randomized quinary baseline.
Chemical short-range order modifies work-hardening behavior relative to the randomized quinary baseline.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can produce a single-phase FCC microstructure in the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its studied quaternary and ternary subsets.
Annealing in a suitable thermal regime allows chemical short-range order to develop without inducing second phases.
The fully equiatomic quinary alloy has near-random mixing and minimal chemical short-range order because of its high chemical complexity.
Near-random mixing in the quinary alloy produces comparatively uniform resistance to dislocation motion.
Reduced constituent variety in the quaternary and ternary subsets permits increased local chemical ordering.
Clusters exhibiting chemical short-range order act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Quaternary and ternary alloys with promoted chemical short-range order will have higher yield strengths than identically processed equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Quaternary and ternary alloys with promoted chemical short-range order will have altered work-hardening rates relative to identically processed equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Mechanical-property differences across the alloy set will correlate with quantitative measurements of chemical short-range order.
The proposed relationship is limited to alloys that retain the FCC phase without significant phase separation or precipitation.
The proposed relationship may not apply when constituent removal induces a different deformation mechanism.
Diffuse scattering or pair-distribution-function analysis can quantitatively assess chemical short-range order in these alloys.
